title: Rethinking Team Building: how a 30-person Startup serves 50 Million Users — Grant Lee, Gamma
talk_summary: Grant Lee, CEO of Gamma, describes how a 30-person team serves 50M users by hiring generalists, using 'player coaches' who both manage and do hands-on work, and investing in culture/transparency.

takeaways.what_they_do: Every core leader is a hands-on 'player coach' who both manages/prioritizes and does the actual work, so decisions are made by someone with deep in-flight context rather than a detached top-down manager.
takeaways.evidence_quote: every single one of them is a player coach... they still love to code. They still love to be in the day-to-day

takeaways.what_they_do: A weekly metrics deep-dive plus a 'wall of work' where everyone shows what they're working on, and twice-weekly company-wide show-and-tell, keeps shared context and surfaces work.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we have this thing called the wall of work where everybody's showing like what everyone else is working on

takeaways.what_they_do: Candidates do the actual job for a trial period (default 3 months) before a full hire, especially for roles where the definition of 'good' is unclear; roles without a work trial had high failure rates.
takeaways.numbers: 5+ work trials, all worked out; high failure rate without

takeaways.what_they_do: They judge agency by asking candidates to walk through the layers of a hard problem and their failed attempts, not just the final solution; people who can't go to second/third-order depth weren't doing the thinking.
takeaways.evidence_quote: if they can articulate what the true problem was... all the attempts at the solution

takeaways.what_they_do: They maintain and continuously rewrite a culture deck reflecting current team values and onboard everyone with it, to preserve shared operating norms as the team grows.
takeaways.evidence_quote: We have a living culture deck that we've maintained basically since the beginning. And we rewrite it all the time.
